name: I/O Module

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the LED starts blinking.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the LED starts blinking.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.
Have the Hub send Get Operating Flags (cmd2 0x00) and note bit 6 (Reverse the sensor), which linking can change.

Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Get Operating Flags again. If bit 6 changed, have it send Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x0E to set it or 0x0F to clear it, as it was before linking.
Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.
Once linked, the Hub reads the device's settings with Get Operating Flags and an extended Get for group 1.

A link to the I/O Linc's relay records the relay's state when it's made. To link the relay to a group of the Hub's own, first set the relay to the state the Hub's On command should give (send On, cmd1 0x11, or Off, cmd1 0x13), turn momentary mode off with Set Operating Flags cmd2 0x07 while linking, and turn it back on with cmd2 0x06 afterward.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
If the Hub also controls the I/O Linc from a group of its own, have the Hub start unlinking for that group (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder, for group 0; the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09), as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

notes: Has one relay, with normally open, normally closed and common contacts, and two sense inputs.
The relay's momentary mode can be set from 1 second to 30 minutes.
An I/O Module Expander, which has no Insteon radio of its own, adds four more zones.
